results.evidence: Retry found only segment figures: the North Fork Quinault trail to Low Divide is about 16 mi with roughly 3,100 ft of gain, and one trip report gives about 2,100 ft from a Low Divide-area camp to the 5,600 ft north saddle. No source states a car-to-car total for the out-and-back climb, so neither 7,000 nor 8,000+ ft can be confirmed. Would be settled by a trip report or route page giving the round-trip gain for North Fork Quinault to Christie and back.

No new source found describing September conditions on the North Couloir/Christie Glacier route; documented ascents remain late July to mid-August, and cascadeclimbers and summitpost pages did not load. Would be settled by two late-season (September) reports stating whether the couloir is melted out or still efficient.

The only source giving numbers is one trip report: one 60-foot rappel 'with 55 feet of rope' off the summit block. Steven Song's party climbed and downclimbed the summit block without a rope, and Lucas's report mentions no rappel; no second source gives the rappel height or rope length. Would be settled by a second party stating the rappel height or the rope length they used.

A 2025 WTA trip report says the party had to 'downclimb a class 3 crack' where the ledge seems to cliff out, with a cairn at its top (the same feature the hazards line describes). Steven Song's independent report calls the same spot, reached from the SE ridge, 'exposed 3rd class down-climbing on slabs'. One other report says 3+ or 4 at its hardest bit, but two independent parties agree on Class 3, so beta, hazards and the ROUTE BREAKDOWN row all become Class 3.
